title.en: Explain why early diagnosis needs molecular methods
Describe the use of PCR, DNA probes and ELISA in diagnosis

say.en: By the time a patient feels ill, the virus or bacterium has multiplied a lot. Molecular tests can find it when only a few copies are present. In this lesson: Explain why early diagnosis needs molecular methods.
Describe the use of PCR, DNA probes and ELISA in diagnosis.

body.en: Effective treatment needs early *diagnosis* and an understanding of the pathophysiology. Conventional methods (serum and urine analysis) cannot detect a pathogen early, because by then its concentration is already high. Very low concentrations of a bacterium or virus, before symptoms appear, can be detected by amplifying its nucleic acid by PCR. PCR is now routinely used to detect HIV in suspected AIDS patients and to detect mutations in genes in suspected cancer patients, and it is a powerful technique to identify many other genetic disorders. A single-stranded DNA or RNA tagged with a radioactive molecule (a probe) is allowed to hybridise to its complementary DNA in a clone of cells, followed by detection using autoradiography. The clone with the mutated gene will not appear on the photographic film, because the probe is not complementary to the mutated gene.

points.en: PCR detects pathogens at very low concentration
Used for HIV in suspected AIDS patients and gene mutations in cancer
Radioactive probe + autoradiography; mutated gene does not show up

narration.en: PCR amplifies a pathogen's nucleic acid so it can be detected even at very low levels, for example HIV in suspected AIDS patients. A radioactive probe binds its complementary DNA, and a mutated gene does not show up on the autoradiograph.
narration.kn: PCR ರೋಗಕಾರಕದ ನ್ಯೂಕ್ಲಿಕ್ ಆಮ್ಲವನ್ನು ವರ್ಧಿಸಿ ಅತಿ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಪ್ರಮಾಣದಲ್ಲೂ ಪತ್ತೆಹಚ್ಚುತ್ತದೆ, ಉದಾ. ಶಂಕಿತ AIDS ರೋಗಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ HIV. ವಿಕಿರಣಶೀಲ ಪ್ರೋಬ್ ಪೂರಕ DNA ಗೆ ಅಂಟುತ್ತದೆ; ಉತ್ಪರಿವರ್ತಿತ ಜೀನ್ ಆಟೋರೇಡಿಯೋಗ್ರಾಫ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಕಾಣುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

Older tests find a disease only after symptoms appear. Molecular tests find the pathogen when only a little of it is present.
PCR copies the pathogen DNA until there is enough to detect. The more DNA we start with, the fewer cycles it takes to cross the detection line.
A probe is a labelled single-stranded DNA or RNA. It binds its complementary sequence, and autoradiography shows where. A mutated gene does not bind, so it does not show up.
ELISA works on antigen-antibody binding. An enzyme linked to the antibody makes a colour, so a coloured well means a positive test.

text.en: Amplifies a very low amount of bacterial or viral nucleic acid
Routinely used to detect HIV in suspected AIDS patients
Detects mutations in genes of suspected cancer patients
A tagged single strand hybridises to its complementary DNA in a clone
Autoradiography: a clone with the mutated gene does not appear on the film
Based on the principle of antigen–antibody interaction
Detects antigens such as proteins and glycoproteins of a pathogen
Detects antibodies the body has made against a pathogen

explanation.en: PCR amplifies tiny amounts of a pathogen's nucleic acid, so it can detect HIV in suspected AIDS patients and gene mutations in suspected cancer patients before symptoms. A radioactively tagged single-stranded DNA or RNA probe hybridises to its complementary DNA in a clone; a clone with a mutated gene does not show up on the photographic film. ELISA works by antigen–antibody interaction, detecting the pathogen's antigens or the antibodies made against it.

tagline.en: PCR, ELISA and probes for early diagnosis; uses of transgenic animals; GEAC, patents and biopiracy of basmati, neem and turmeric.

say.en: Animals whose DNA has been manipulated to carry and express an extra (foreign) gene are transgenic. Rats, rabbits, pigs, sheep, cows and fish have been made, but over 95% are mice.

The Indian Government set up the GEAC (Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee) to decide on the validity of GM research and the safety of introducing GM organisms for public services. Biopiracy is the use of bio-resources by multinational companies without proper authorisation from the countries and people concerned and without compensatory payment.

homework.en: Make a table comparing PCR, DNA probes and ELISA: what each detects and its principle.

narration.en: Recap. Early diagnosis needs detection at low pathogen concentration. PCR detects HIV and cancer mutations by amplifying nucleic acids. Radioactive probes and autoradiography identify mutated genes. ELISA detects antigens or antibodies.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ಮುಂಚಿತ ರೋಗನಿರ್ಣಯಕ್ಕೆ ಕಡಿಮೆ ರೋಗಕಾರಕ ಸಾಂದ್ರತೆಯಲ್ಲೇ ಪತ್ತೆ ಅಗತ್ಯ. PCR ನ್ಯೂಕ್ಲಿಕ್ ಆಮ್ಲ ವರ್ಧಿಸಿ HIV ಮತ್ತು ಕ್ಯಾನ್ಸರ್ ಉತ್ಪರಿವರ್ತನೆಗಳನ್ನು ಪತ್ತೆಹಚ್ಚುತ್ತದೆ. ವಿಕಿರಣಶೀಲ ಪ್ರೋಬ್ ಮತ್ತು ಆಟೋರೇಡಿಯೋಗ್ರಫಿ ಉತ್ಪರಿವರ್ತಿತ ಜೀನ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಗುರುತಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ELISA ಪ್ರತಿಜನಕ ಅಥವಾ ಪ್ರತಿಕಾಯಗಳನ್ನು ಪತ್ತೆಹಚ್ಚುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Let us recall the key ideas. Early diagnosis needs detection at low pathogen concentration.
say.kn: ಮುಖ್ಯ ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳೋಣ. ಮುಂಚಿತ ರೋಗನಿರ್ಣಯಕ್ಕೆ ಕಡಿಮೆ ರೋಗಕಾರಕ ಸಾಂದ್ರತೆಯಲ್ಲೇ ಪತ್ತೆ ಅಗತ್ಯ.
